name: Press Sheet
blurb: Straight off the press, over the one piece of production furniture that still reads at thumbnail size: the ink bar.

name: Letterpress
blurb: Ink and impression. The plate struck deep into cotton stock, paper lipping up around the bite.

name: Hot Foil
blurb: Stamped in metal on dark linen board. Each half keeps its own hue, translated into a single directional foil sweep.

name: Ben Day
blurb: A coarse mechanical dot screen run edge to edge, clearing around the mark's own silhouette.

name: Die Cut
blurb: The mark cut clean through a paper disc, with a two-tone board underneath returning the brand colours.

name: Reverse
blurb: A solid flood of BHD cyan with the mark lifted straight out of it to bare stock, and a yellow trap along one edge.

name: Module
blurb: The mark is drawn on a 30.41-unit square grid. This lays that grid back over the sheet and fills four of its cells.

name: Brayer
blurb: One pass of a hand roller. The band runs off both sides, so only its torn top and bottom edges are in frame.

name: Stamp
blurb: A two-pad rubber stamp struck once on kraft. Two pads, because one ink fuses the Arabic and Latin blocks.

name: Midnight
blurb: Nothing but the mark, full colour, on tinted near-black, inside one hairline that echoes the circular crop.
